weathered.note: THE LETTERING IS A LAYER, NOT THE PLATE (doc 35 section 6). The plate's board is blank; this is the shipping gilt art scaled to the board, dulled and flaked by a seeded erosion: 'the only sign in town that has been painted twice', peeling.

ordinary.note: A framed board on the wall of the small structure under the Clarion's porch, the frame in the plate's own post wood with a cast shadow, so the papers read as a board and not as a papered wall fused into the next building (Tyler, Phase 1.5).

funeral.note: Act III. The same frame plus the authored clean white sheet (posted-notices-act3.png at the plate's scale) pinned over the papers: 'Frame has finally found a spelling he cannot get wrong.' Set by doc 48's S2.

filled.note: THE CANONICAL TROUGH, PHASE 1.5B: local prop art painted IN CONTEXT by the one owner-authorized operation (art/staging/room-02/trough-01/trough-op.json), cut by an authored polygon (tools/retrofit/trough-extract.py) and seated beside the east hitching rail with its footprint in the mid mud. entrances.note: the east edge, by the road in, facing down the street

say: Half of it is two stories tall in front and one story deep.
The other half is real, and is doing better.
onEnterSay.note: His first sight of the town, and the words come from doc 05's THE FALSE FRONTS rather than being written fresh -- he has the opinion already; this is him having it out loud at the moment he first has it. AMENDED AFTER TYLER CHECKED IT AGAINST THE PLATE: the original said EVERY building was a false front, which the picture contradicts -- the saloon is a flat parapet with a low roof behind it, and the hotel beside it is genuinely two storeys with lit windows and real depth. The plate is signed off, so the writing yields, and the observation is better for it: the half that is real is the half with money, which is the town's whole economy in one line. Gated on T_SEEN_MAIN_STREET, which onEnter sets, so it plays once.

obstacles.note: THE NEAR HITCHING RAIL at the west end: a foreground object he cannot walk through. It is the occluder this street never had; until its mask is cut from an ACCEPTED plate he walks round it, not behind it.

onEnterWalkNote: OUT INTO THE ROAD, NOT ALONG THE BUILDINGS. He was walking to x3400 y640, which is the boardwalk edge in front of the claims-road exit and beside the map seller’s office -- he arrived and then sidled up against a wall. x3300 y706 is the middle of the street with the town in front of him, which is where a man stands when he has just walked into a town he has never seen. Clear of the assay office door at x3082-3144, clear of the map seller at x3140, and low enough to be in the road rather than on the walk.
